title_as_printed: Experimental Boiling Point Elevations of Concentrated NaCl Solutions at Higher Temperatures
pressure_note: Boiling point elevation at constant pressure = vapor pressure of the solution at the isotherm; the 'Pure Water Boiling Temperature' column is the saturation temperature of pure water at that pressure (Keenan and Keyes tables, text section 5.3.7/8.4). Pressure itself is not tabulated.
conversion_needs: solution temperature = pure-water boiling temperature + B.P.E. (equals the nominal isotherm 75, 100,... 300 C); pressure = vapor pressure of water at the pure-water boiling temperature (steam tables)
notes: BPE values were derived by the authors from the vapor pressure lowering measurements (same measurements as Table 2, concentrations agree to 3-4 digits). Printed as two side-by-side blocks (left 70-188 C, right 185-288 C); stacked left then right. Row 115.396 / 6.9350 / 9.726: the sum 125.122 differs from the 125 C isotherm of the neighbouring rows (all other rows sum to the isotherm within 0.001): probable misprint in BPE (125 - 115.396 = 9.604), kept as printed.
